verdict.rationale: Runpod documents Instant Clusters as fully managed multi-node compute where you can deploy jobs without managing infrastructure or cluster configuration. That covers the story's goal of not running your own cluster. However, no evidence names Slurm, Kubernetes, or any managed job scheduler or queue. missing for 10: explicit managed Slurm support, explicit managed Kubernetes support, documented job scheduling/queueing semantics, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes

citations.quote: Instant Clusters provide fully managed multi-node compute with high-performance networking for distributed workloads.
Deploy jobs or large-scale without managing infrastructure, networking, or cluster configuration.
